lines.text: Someone mailed him a steel box bolted shut with a coffee can welded inside.
And inside is a can of 1950s motor oil so would it still protect an engine?
He cooks it at 410 degrees right next to modern oil.
And the old oil loses 42 percent more weight so it's literally cooking off into the air.
In a minus forty freezer it barely moves.
And after an engine run the cylinder head is crusty because oil that can't take heat bakes onto hot metal.
The lab report shows why because there's just 6 parts per million of calcium.
Calcium is the detergent that grabs soot and acid so without it everything turns to sludge.
And its acid fighting reserve is zero point four versus six point two for modern oil which is fifteen times less.
So it still lubricates but it's like a shield that's already used up and your engine would sludge fast.
So would you put it in your car?
